h: The artists who put St Ives on the map
p: The gallery opened in 1993 and was given a major extension in 2017, adding more space for exhibitions. Its focus is on the artists who made St Ives famous in the 20th century, and some names are worth knowing before you go.

Ben Nicholson and Barbara Hepworth moved to St Ives at the start of the Second World War, and they helped turn the town into a hub for abstract art. Patrick Heron, Terry Frost and Peter Lanyon were among the other big names linked with the town. Then there is Alfred Wallis, a retired fisherman who started painting in his later years, using scraps of card and ship's paint. His simple, heartfelt boats and harbours inspired the professional artists around him, and his story is a lovely one to share.
In the entrance area, look out for Patrick Heron's large coloured-glass window, which glows beautifully when the sun catches it.

Allow an hour or two for the gallery, and add time for the Hepworth Museum, which is a must if you have the energy. Sculpture fans will also enjoy the Leach Pottery, founded by Bernard Leach, a short walk up the hill.

Parking in St Ives can be tricky in high season, so many visitors take the scenic St Ives Bay Line train from St Erth instead. It hugs the coast and offers gorgeous views of Carbis Bay along the way. Once in town, Porthmeor Beach is right below the gallery for a paddle or a spot of surf-watching, and the harbour is a short stroll away for a pasty on the wall.
